findings.claim: (3) Rights are NOT passed through a BFF at all — there is no server proxy route in this codebase (`find src/routes -iname '*+server*'` and `-type d -iname api` both empty). The app is a pure client-side SPA (`ssr = false`, JWT in localStorage) that calls Entu directly with the signed-in user's own Bearer token; Entu itself enforces write rights server-side, and the app only reads back `_owner`/`_editor` reference lists on the entity to decide whether to SHOW management controls (`manageRightsFrom`/`resolveManageRights`). A parent-event editor creating a schedule_item is therefore just that user's own JWT hitting Entu's create endpoint directly — no elevated/service-account or BFF-mediated write path exists for this.

findings.claim: AXIS(5) — a '·' middle-dot separator already has a live precedent on the event detail page's tally line with no known locale collision issue raised against it, and all four locale files (en/et/lv/uk) exist under messages/.
findings.evidence: src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:2298-2306 uses a bare `·` between tally `<span>`s (`{m.event_detail_tally_maybe(...)}` … `·` … `{m.event_detail_tally_late(...)}`); `ls messages` → en.json, et.json, lv.json, uk.json.

findings.claim: AXIS(5)/spec-fragility — AgendaList.spec.ts's existing time assertions use `querySelectorAll('span').map(textContent).toContain/not.toContain(...)` (containment, not exhaustive-count), so an ADDITIONAL span for a times-line is not structurally forbidden by these specific assertions — but a future schedule-item render that emits a bare clock-only span (e.g. a schedule item whose own time renders as a standalone '09:30' span rather than folded into one 'time name' string) could collide with the existing `.not.toContain('09:30')` / `.not.toContain('19:00')`-style negative assertions.
findings.evidence: src/lib/components/agenda/AgendaList.spec.ts:775,807 `const spanTexts = [...recentRow!.querySelectorAll('span')].map((s) => s.textContent?.trim()); expect(spanTexts).toContain('9:30 AM'); expect(spanTexts).not.toContain('09:30');` — this is a containment check over ALL spans in the row, so a new span's exact text matters.

findings.claim: AXIS(6) — no auth/protected-route gate exists on the event detail route itself; token absence is passed through to Entu as `''` and Entu's own `_sharing` rules are the actual authority, so an anonymous caller hitting schedule_item (domain-shared, same as program_item) will get the same 401/403→session-expired/load-error classification the page already applies uniformly — no new rights branch is needed for anonymous handling.
findings.evidence: src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:10-12 comment ('No `getToken()`-missing gate … the token is threaded straight through to Entu, which is the actual authority on whether it's valid') and :302 `const cfg = { db: current.db, token: getToken() ?? '' };`.

findings.claim: AXIS(6) — the single rights predicate `manageRightsFrom(ownerIds, editorIds, personId)` (owner-OR-editor) already drives BOTH the tally visibility and the Works-section editor controls on this page; schedule_item's identical rights posture (per docs/architecture/mvox-schema-extensions.md:53-55, 76-79) means it should reuse this SAME predicate/`isEditor` derivation rather than invent a parallel rights check.
findings.evidence: src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:262-268 `function canSeeTally(d, personId) { return manageRightsFrom(d.ownerIds, d.editorIds, personId) === 'editor'; }` and :270-272 `const isEditor = $derived(...)`; docs/architecture/mvox-schema-extensions.md:53-55 '`Rights posture: identical to program_item — whoever holds _editor+ on the parent event … can create/edit schedule items.`'

findings.claim: AXIS(7) — no code branch distinguishing invite-created vs auto-provisioned persons was found affecting EVENT rights resolution; event/schedule_item rights derive purely from `_owner`/`_editor` refs on the event/season entities (conductor/admin roles) plus domain `_sharing`, independent of how the person/member entity was created.
findings.evidence: Searched src/lib/roster/memberLifecycle.ts, src/lib/invite/{redeem,inviteData}.ts existence (grep -rln 'auto-provision|invitation' found these three non-spec files) but did not find any conditional in eventDetail.ts, entuSeasons.ts, or rosterData.ts keyed on invite-vs-auto-provisioned provenance for event/schedule_item read/write rights.

risks: The event detail page's `loadForSelected` generation guard is hand-rolled inline (not routeLoad.ts) — a schedule_item load added carelessly (e.g. fired from a different function without capturing `g` at call time, mirroring the `writeGenerations`/tally pattern) could re-introduce a stale-collective-switch race even though the surrounding page already has the idiom to copy correctly.

schedule_item's per-db type id genuinely differs (polyphony 6a9ccea4ca67df980f4173c5 vs mvox_crede 6a9cceabca67df980f4173ee) — ANY hardcoded id literal (copy-pasted from a seed-result JSON during dev/testing) would silently work on one collective and 403/404 on the other; the fix is strict adherence to the existing `_type.string=schedule_item` query convention, with no exception review found that permits raw ids in src/.

AgendaMonthView.svelte and AgendaList.svelte share the exact same `filteredAgendaItems` array from one producer; if a future implementer adds schedule-item data onto the shared `AgendaItem` type (rather than a separate `scheduleItemsByEventId` record passed ONLY to `<AgendaList>`, mirroring how `worksByEventId`/`worksManage` are already NOT passed to `<AgendaMonthView>`), the #247 'exactly four things, no time' fence becomes only a template-level guarantee, not a data-level one — a later edit to AgendaMonthView.svelte would then have the schedule data sitting right there to accidentally render.

The event-detail-time regex assertions (`.match(/19:00/g)).toHaveLength(1)`, `.match(/7:00 PM/g)).toHaveLength(1)`) are scoped to the `event-detail-time` element specifically — this is SAFE only if the new schedule-item list is NOT nested inside that same element/testid; if an implementer folds the chronological list into the existing time block instead of giving it its own section/testid, these exact tests break the first time a schedule item's own clock reading matches the event's start time (a very likely fixture case, e.g. a 'Performance' item at the event's own start_datetime).

No evidence was found (nor explicitly ruled out) of a distinct rights path for invite-created vs auto-provisioned persons on event/schedule_item visibility — this axis is reported as 'not found' rather than 'confirmed absent'; memberLifecycle.ts/inviteData.ts/redeem.ts were not read in full and could still hold a provenance-conditional branch relevant to event rights that this sweep did not surface.

The full battery of agenda +page.svelte specs that render AgendaList/AgendaMonthView end-to-end (page.agenda-filter.spec.ts, page.agenda-admin.spec.ts, page.agenda-event-types.spec.ts, page.works-wiring.spec.ts, page.attendance-*.spec.ts, page.conductor-wiring.spec.ts, page.season-manage.spec.ts, page.season-create.spec.ts) were located but NOT individually inspected for exact-count/snapshot assertions that additive schedule elements could break — listed as candidates for the mechanical(1) sweep but unverified beyond their existence.
